prompt: A gym charges a $\$25$ sign-up fee plus $\$10$ per month. Write an equation for the total cost $y$ after $x$ months.
hint: One cost is paid a single time and the other is paid again every month. Decide which is the start and which is the rate.

hints.text: One cost is paid a single time and the other is paid again every month. Decide which is the start and which is the rate.
The sign-up fee is the starting value $b = 25$ and the monthly charge is the slope $m = 10$. Put them into $y = mx + b$.
With slope $10$ and starting value $25$, the equation is $y = 10x + 25$.

explanation: At zero months you have already paid the sign-up fee, so the starting value is $b = 25$.
Every month adds another $10$ dollars to the total, so the slope is $m = 10$.
Putting these into $y = mx + b$ gives the equation $y = 10x + 25$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Check with 3 months
steps: The equation gives $10 \times 3 + 25 = 55$ — it checks out.
